findings.reason: The protected source is the conventional fixed-window ring design: it aggregates same-second hits, resets a slot on timestamp-cycle reuse, and sums only live slots. Its class and app adapter are clear, concise, and expert interview-quality, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 362 and its Python HitCounter surface. The Reference preserves chronological calls, repeated same-second hits, the open-left 300-second window, the source operation sequence and explanation, all three constraints, and the high-volume same-second follow-up.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064603055. Its two fixed arrays, modulo slot selection, timestamp mismatch reset, same-timestamp increment, live-window predicate, and sum are identical to the protected HitCounter apart from the app-local operation adapter.

The former 512- and 2048-operation benchmark tiers exceeded the 300-call source constraint and were removed. The replacement bounded-domain certificate proves one-slot hit updates, exactly 300 query inspections, and fixed 600-entry storage; its regression passes the app and native implementations for no-hit queries, every age from 0 through 300, slot reuse, and 299 same-second hits plus one query at the legal call limit.

The Approach accurately derives the 300-slot timestamp ring, explains why reuse resets counts, proves the live-window predicate, and distinguishes per-hit aggregation from unbounded per-hit history. Its O(1) time and space bounds correctly treat the source-fixed 300-second window as constant.

The hash-bound authenticated Premium Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including the complete source operation trace, exact timestamp and call-count constraints, chronological-order guarantee, interval boundary, and source-native scalability follow-up.

coverage: The sole authenticated Premium source example is now one complete first case with its exact seven method calls and three app-adapter query results; the former partial samples are correctly labelled trials.
Visible timestamp coverage includes the legal minimum 1, the maximum 2,000,000,000, and hit ages 299 and 300 that distinguish inclusion from exact expiry.
Queries before any hit, repeated hits in one second, modulo-slot reuse, mixed bursts, multiple queries, and fully expired history exercise every state transition.

An independent append-only hit-history oracle verified all nine authored results, 18,943 exhaustive chronological streams, every possible hit age from 0 through 300, and 299 same-second hits plus one query at the 300-call limit.

All nine correctness cases are visible samples or trials. benchmark.json remains absent, and the unchanged bounded-domain certificate separately proves fixed work and storage for the source-fixed 300-second window.
